title: BenchmarkDotNet
description: The standard .NET library for reliable micro-benchmarking and performance testing.

data.text: `BenchmarkDotNet` automates the process of running micro-benchmarks. It handles warm-up, iteration, statistical analysis, and generates detailed reports.
Mark a method with `[Benchmark]` and run it with `BenchmarkRunner.Run<T>()`.

data.title: Simple Benchmark

data.text: BenchmarkDotNet automatically compares all `[Benchmark]` methods and prints a summary table with mean, error, and allocation data.

data.title: Warning
data.text: BenchmarkDotNet is for micro-benchmarks. Always profile real workloads for performance analysis.
Measuring Without the Compiler Lying to You

BenchmarkDotNet runs each method many times in an isolated process, warms up the JIT, and reports not just the mean but the distribution and allocations. It exists because a simple `Stopwatch` loop is unreliable: the JIT can eliminate code whose result is unused, and the first iterations are dominated by warm-up.

data.title: A benchmark comparing two implementations
Interview angle: measure, then optimize
data.text: The disciplined answer to "is this fast enough" is to measure with a benchmark, find the hot path with a profiler, change one thing, and measure again. BenchmarkDotNet also reports allocations, which matters because an allocation on a hot path becomes GC pressure and a latency spike under load. Optimizing from intuition is how you make code slower and less readable at the same time.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `[Benchmark]` to mark methods to measure.
BenchmarkDotNet handles warm-up, statistics, and reporting.
data.takeaway: BenchmarkDotNet is the gold standard for reliable .NET micro-benchmarking.
